newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND RECALL ANDREW TO SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND RECALL ANDREW TO SQUAD.

text.p: England have recalled 34-year-old fly-half Rob Andrew to their squad for Saturday's Five Nations' championship finale against Wales in Cardiff.
Andrew, director of rugby at Newcastle, retired from international rugby at the start of last season after winning 70 caps.
His surprise selection is a result of increasing concern over first choice fly-half Paul Grayson who has a torn muscle in his hip.

Mike Catt, who held the position before Christmas, is expected to play if Grayson is not fit but Andrew, England's all-time record points scorer with 396 from 1985-1995, gives coach Jack Rowell another option.
Andrew said on Wednesday he had been asked to join the squad as cover for Grayson but emphasised he was not making a comeback to international rugby.
''As far as I am concerned, I certainly don't expect to play,'' he said. ''This is very much a one-off, I certainly don't expect to make a comeback.''
England, beaten 23-20 by France at Twickenham on March 1, must beat Wales to secure the Triple Crown.
